text_fidelity_a:
Impact Custom Professional MMA/Boxing/Muay Thai Mouthguard White This is the best mouthguard I’ve ever used. I’ll get that out of the way now. It’s very comfortable, and very thick and protective as well. It is so well fit that it has a sort of suction effect on the teeth so it won’t fall out. Love it.

The reason for the 3 stars: The reputation the company has for communication throughout the process is one of the reasons I bought. I wasn’t sure if I should try this or spend twice the money with my dentist, and I almost went with my dentist for the fact that I’d have somebody helping me.

When I took my mold, I emailed the photos to Impact as they recommend and got a reply pretty quick. That’s great. But that was the end of the communication. They’ve said in their promotional materials that they send an email when your mold arrives, and that they advise when the mouthguard is on the way. I didn’t receive any of this. I actually became concerned that my order was lost in the mail on the way to Impact after a week and a half or so, so I had to email to ask if it arrived. The following day it was confirmed, and I was told the turnaround was about 2 weeks from receiving and that I would get an email when it went out. I didn’t get that email either. But after about 3 weeks from when I sent the mold, my mouthguard arrived and it’s awesome.

If I lose this one or need another, I’ll buy Impact again. This said, I hope they see my review and step their communication game back up. I may very well be just a rare anecdotal case, and the product is great, but I didn’t expect to find myself wondering if my mold had gotten lost in the mail.
text_fidelity_b: Impact Custom Professional MMA/Boxing/Muay Thai Mouthguard White

text_fidelity_a:
Smith & Wesson Extraction and Evasion SW671 15.9in Full Tang Tomahawk with a 3.9in Steel Blade and TPE Handle for Outdoor, Tactical, Survival and EDC For what it is, and for the price I paid, this is a sturdy and well-made full tang hawk that will blow through most things that get in its way. It is elegantly designed as a working tool to help get you out of tight spots. Being a one piece chunk of steel with a comfortable handle fastened to the shaft with four bolts, this is not a flimsy tool that will fly apart when confronted with heavy work. It is well-balanced and comfortable to hold with either one or two hands. It's also big enough to allow choking up if you need more control and a shorter stroke.

Its uses are virtually endless. Because of its solid construction and reasonable price, I wouldn't hesitate to use it in any situation. The chances of this breaking are slim and even if it does, you're only out about $30.00. Very few tomohawk makers have a straight spike on the opposite end of the blade. There are a few situations that I can think of where you would use the spike but would have to rapidly pull it out before striking again. It won't do you any good to kill a zombie and have your hawk stuck in its skull. Of course that would only happen with a fresh one, an older model will be brittle and your spike should blow right through it.

This hawk came sharp but didn't pass the paper test. A little extra elbow grease and that can be rectified. It's weight might be a little restrictive for people without much arm strength and it might be a bear to carry all day if hiking. The sheath that comes with it will cover the axe head and ride on your belt. Just don't expect that to work too well for you. This ideally would be carried in your vehilcle and used when unexpected circumstances arise. Even if you don't know what you're doing with it, just holding it will inspire confidenc. And often times attitude can be the tipping point in getting any job done.
text_fidelity_b: Smith & Wesson Extraction and Evasion SW671 15.9in Full Tang Tomahawk with a 3.9in Steel Blade and TPE Handle for Outdoor, Tactical, Survival and EDC

text_fidelity_a:
Omron HJ-112 Digital Pocket Pedometer I have been using this pedometer for 4 weeks now, and it works great.
The pros:
It comes with a clip and tether. You can clip it or put it in your pocket. You can even clip it to your purse, but I like it on my pants so I can count every single step of the day.
It counts steps, distance, calories. Don't ask me if they are all accurate. I'm only tracking steps and working towards a goal.
You can look back up to a week of steps, in case you are keeping track.
It resets every midnight (no, it never turns off).
Small enough to fit in a pocket.
The cons:
Well, con. Only one up to now. I tried hooking it to my bra or neckline (sometimes I wear dresses) and it doesn't record steps very accurately. I'll be walking for 10 minutes and the number of steps doesn't change. So on dress days, I hook it to my purse, or my underwear if the dress is baggy.

In the last 4 weeks I've gone from an average of 4,000 steps per day to 7,000 steps! It's fun to keep track.
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ-112 Digital Pocket Pedometer

If you need smaller, then you need a flashlight! As for light, it has plenty! I have 2 LED lanterns 10" tall by 5" dia. and they put out half as much light as these smaller ones. My bigger ones are not efficient enough to read by, these are. I need these strictly for outages, which we seem to have a lot of, and I appreciate the area coverage of these. No, it will not make it easy to read a few feet away from them, no lantern does that, but it will make it easy to see and navigate in a 15' x 15' room.
They are adjustable in only one way, and that is how much you open them. (At just high enough to turn them on, they make great guiding lights for a footpath or a cluttered area.) All the bulbs are on no matter how close to closed it is, so there is no power saving advantage to having it lowered. 12 Hours of emergency or evening lighting outside, is a lot of hours! It will more than stand up to all emergency needs except getting lost in a cave! LOL If it only had 3-4 hours of good light, I would not be happy with this, my first thought is always 'how to extend the emergency light time' and 'is it adjustable'. Well, you can't, and its not....Because of that this would not be an economic idea for an extended camping trip. But this is not being touted as a night after night lighting fix, as an emergency light, I don't need to worry about that.
I joined Etekcity's review program, because I have purchased several of their products and haven't found one I didn't appreciate a lot! As such I don't feel bad about getting one of their products at a reduced price or free for reviewing them. I take my time, and look at all the negative reviews and see if any apply to the product i received. So far.... yes it is pretty light, but no it would not blow away in less that 50mph winds. And i don't think you would be outside enjoying an evening in that kind of wind anyway. It has the hard anodized look and feeling of a well coated flashlight. The handles are wide enough to be easy to carry and a bungee cord or rope will attach them to the side of any tree or post, or you can hang them from a limb or tent pole. Heavy enough not to tip over, and good quality plastic instead of glass or cheep plastic that cracks. I don't see anything cheap or flimsy feeling about them at all!
Don't know what else to say about these, except my other two larger ones are going out into storage and I will be getting 2 more of these to store inside for emergencies. I highly recommend them!
PS: If you DO get a lemon, for Pete's sake tell them! They are very quick and easy to talk to. There is a card in the box with a toll free number, their e-mail address and their website on it (etekcity.com).... all for customer support.

text_fidelity_a:
Planet Bike Beamer 3 Bike Headlight This light has two practical safety functions:

It helps make your presence on the road more apparent to on coming traffic. The light is bright enough from even a few hundred feet that a driver would have to be extremely oblivious and distracted not to see it.

Perhaps more importantly, the light will illuminate street signs and signals that are made with a reflective material at distances of over 450 feet away (I measured using google maps). When I first used the light (in flashing mode), I was genuinely shocked to see how the street signs up to two blocks ahead of me were pulsating. I say that this is important because it helps you spot stop signs in the distance - assuming you're being a safe cyclist, biking in a lane, with traffic, abiding by traffic laws, you're probably most likely to get killed by accidently running a stop sign. When I bike home from work at night, I take streets that have no traffic lights and only stop signs, so being able to spot them is very important for me.

The light attaches to your handle bar through via a mount; the light can easily slid off the mount so you don't have to bike around with it during the day, nor leave it on the bike when it's parked outside.

The light does what it needs to do for a reasonable price. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.

text_fidelity_a:
Hand Warmers Rechargeable, 2 Pack Electric Magnetic Portable Hand Warmer,Reusable 10000mAh Power Bank, 360° Heating & Max 15Hrs Warmth Time, 3 Levels Temp, Women, Men I own four other hand warmers, all of them one-piece batteries. At a first glance, this hand warmer looks very similar, but you soon realize it has double the number of ports and buttons of a typical hand warmer. And that’s because this one warmer is actually two halves attached magnetically. You can use it as a single unit, with both sides heating, or you can split it into two independent halves and put each half in a different hand or pocket, or use one half as a warmer and the other half to charge your phone. The caveat is that the external, rounded part of each half is the only one that heats. The internal, flat part that can attach to the other half magnetically does not produce heat. I don’t think that’s a downside. If you are holding one of the halves of the warmer in the palm of your hand, the heating side perfectly fits your palm, and the flat side is only covered by your fingertips, so any heat would be wasted anyway.

Each half warmer has a 5000mAh battery, so in theory you have a combined 10000mAh.

Bottomline: I like the concept of two independent batteries that are shaped so they can also function as a single unit. That concept distinguishes this warmer from the other four I own.
text_fidelity_b: Hand Warmers Rechargeable, 2 Pack Electric Magnetic Portable Hand Warmer,Reusable 10000mAh Power Bank, 360° Heating & Max 15Hrs Warmth Time, 3 Levels Temp, Women, Men

Cutter 66384 Camping-Candles, pack of 1, silver If you take the time to research the product, regardless of who markets it, you will find that citronella, as a mosquito repellent, does not, will not, CAN NOT do what it is advertised to do.
The best mosquito repellent is a slight breeze. These insects have extreme difficulty flying/navigating in the slightest breeze.

The reason you see dead mosquitoes in the wax, flame (or light of most types) attracts them. When they fly into the flame, wings, antennaeI, and proboscis get burned off. They fall into the hot wax, and die.

I buy these, locally, to use while fishing. Buy only for the light provided.
To sum it up: people have been told, for decades, that citronella repels mosquitoes, they are persuaded that it works, not noticing a slight breeze, in stead it’s, “Oh, my word! This stuff works!!!”
Do some research. Read a bit. And save your money.
Type in your search engine: how citronella works.
Be amazed !!!
text_fidelity_b: Cutter 66384 Camping-Candles, pack of 1, silver

A regular sized towel
A small 80-piece first aid kit

A 4-pack of D batteries

And I still could have packed a whole other change of clothes EASILY.

In the 30l bag I got the same things in it PLUS
4 bottles of water
A box of cliff bars
Two changes of baby clothes
35 diapers

The owner, Scott, emailed me when i bought my product, when it shipped (generic yet helpful emails) and when I replied to his 3rd email after getting my bags saying I loved them and he sent me a personal message back. I am very impressed. I hope to do more business with this company in the future and would recommend them.

Zero Tolerance 0456, Sinkevich Pocket Knife; 3.25” CPM-20CV Steel Blade, Titanium Handle with Stonewash and Satin Finish, KVT Ball-Bearing Opening, Titanium Frame Lock, Reversible Pocketclip; 6.6 OZ,Silver Not familiar with the PARA Warthog? It is a short, stubby, relatively heavy .45 acp semi auto pistol available in stainless steel.. While it won't win any beauty contests, it has a presence all its own and the intimidation factor it provides is awesome. It's the kind of weapon that when you run out of ammo you can hit your opponent in the face with it for the game winner.

This ZT 0456 has that kind of look to it. It has some (short and stubby) curves but the overall construction is what draws attention to itself. Yes, it is a bit on the (slightly) heavy side, but this knife wasn't designed to be slim and beautiful. It is designed to work, and work hard, taking on any task from cutting to prying that you come up against. How many knives do you have in your collection that can be carried in your pocket, can dispatch any simple cutting jobs with aplomb, and then allow you to pry open a door with it. Most EDC blades don't have the spine for it, much less the overall design and build that would allow even attempting that task.

As I have aged I have learned that a knife should be much more than just a cutting tool. None of my automatic knives can even approach the type of hard work that this Zero Tolerance knife can conquer. The blade is sharp but heavy, the locking mechanism is tight and solid, and the flipper works like butter. People notice it when I pull it from my pocket, not just because it's a knife but because of the attractive and unique design. Everyone wants to know what it is, how much it costs, and where can they "legally" get one. This is one of those places.
text_fidelity_b: Zero Tolerance 0456, Sinkevich Pocket Knife; 3.25” CPM-20CV Steel Blade, Titanium Handle with Stonewash and Satin Finish, KVT Ball-Bearing Opening, Titanium Frame Lock, Reversible Pocketclip; 6.6 OZ,Silver

text_fidelity_a:
Energizer Carabiner LED Area Tent Light As a busy mom on-the-go, this multi-purpose flashlight has come in handy so many times. I clipped it onto my purse when I got it, and thought it would basically be used "for emergencies." Wow. It ended up being so useful for everyday situations, too. When one of the kids got a splinter at a football game, we needed its nice bright light to see well enough to get the pesky splinter out. Of course, it always comes in handy for finding the right key in the dark and unlocking the door. When the light on our garage door opener died, we used this light to maneuver the obstacles in the pitch-black garage. At that point I bought a second one to keep in the car with the First Aid kit.

We used it to find the dog when he takes too long to come in. I used it to quickly signal my husband when he was loaded up with popcorn and couldn't find our seat at the movies! Then, at that point, I decided to just bite the bullet and buy a few more: one to put in our "tornado shelter" area of the basement because where we live the power goes out frequently with bad storms. Candles are OK for adults, but obviously not safe with small kids around, so I bought one for each child (which they promptly "customized" with strips of different color duct tape, so we know whose is whose! When the storms start to get bad, each child gets their Energizer light out, and if the lights go out, they click theirs on. They like to clip it on the belt-loop so they have constant light around them the whole time.

By the way, we also use rechargeable batteries all the time. One of the chargers we use is this one: [[ASIN:B003D7LHJU Rayovac Everyday-Use 4 Position AA/AAA Easy Charger with 2AA and 2AAA OPP Low Self Discharge NiMH batteries]]. It saves us a fortune in batteries, and we can use our Energizer Carabiner lights without worrying about chewing up batteries and cash.

UPDATE: September 27, 2012.
Absolutely LOVE these flashlights! It's been a year since I wrote the initial review, and they are holding up wonderfully, with STEADY use. I'm ordering more today, as I like to give them as gifts, and now I've put one next to every bed. Just a reminder, make sure you use the rechargeable batteries in them (takes 4 AAA batteries) to increase your savings. These buggers are so durable. Dropped numerous times, too. Just can't say enough about them. HIGHEST of recommendations. I only wish I'd found them years ago!
text_fidelity_b: Energizer Carabiner LED Area Tent Light

Pactrade Marine 13 1/2" Destroyer SS 304 Steering Wheel 5 Spoke Teak Wood Cap This is a very nice, solid, sturdy Destroyer wheel. I have a 16 ft. center console and when I replaced the steering gear (steering box, cable) I wanted to put a new wheel on the boat too. The old wheel (heavy emphasis on the word "old") was made of some sort of plasticized hard rubber and it was frankly nasty. Years and years of hand oil, motor oil, motor fuel, fish slime and general grunge had accumulated on and eaten up the wheel. It was time to find a new wheel.

It's hard finding the right size Destroyer wheel because I needed a 13 inch wheel and most of them are bigger. A 13 inch wheel is all that will comfortably clear everything else on the console. Many of the wheels I looked at cost around twice as much as this one did.

The wheels spokes are gathered and locked into a central star and a cover made of what looks like teak wood snaps over the top. The description says "bakelite cover" but mine doesn't look like bakelite, nor does the product picture. Mine looks like the one in the picture. My boat, being a center console, has grab rails around the console but I often find myself using the wheel as a grab hold when moving around on the boat. I'm not a small person, so that's likely considerable stress on the wheel itself. It's not a problem, I've been using this wheel for several months and it's as solid as the day I mounted it.

This wheel is rock solid and a perfect finishing touch for my new steering system. I'm very happy with it and never have hand/fish/oil/fuel/grunge on my helm any more!
text_fidelity_b: Pactrade Marine 13 1/2" Destroyer SS 304 Steering Wheel 5 Spoke Teak Wood Cap

text_fidelity_a:
Igloo Ice Cube, Ocean Blue, 14-can Capacity, 32607 ORIGINAL REVIEW: I replaced my previous Igloo cooler with this one and I really like it. The top compartment is handy. I put a camper type salt shaker in it along with a few other small items. The ice packs that I use fit perfectly and so far the handle seems like it will last. The previous igloo cooler was a bit smaller and was bought in 1992. It still works great except the handle wont stay on so it was time for a new one. I mention this because it's 24 years old and still works. that says a lot for igloo quality. I hope to get that kind of service from this cooler. The only reason the handle failed was because I stumbled and sent the cooler flying. If that had not have happened I probably would not have needed to buy this one. Igloo is rugged, last a long time and with 2 ice packs about the same size as the sides of this cooler, everything stays cool for at least 24 hours as long as it's not in direct sunlight. I'm not one for change, especially when I have a product that works and lasts. I really did need a little larger cooler so yes, I miss the old cooler but not so much because I really like this new one much better. I donated the old one and found it good home. Yes I know it's just a cooler but I used t every work day for 24 years, I got a little attached to it. They still make that model and I nearly bought it but my wife found this new one. Due to the handle issue and the fact this one is way better, I do not recommend the older version any longer in favor for this one. Yes I know run on sentences its 1 am give me a break. Buy this cooler, slap a Cowboys sticker on it and you will be happy with it.

UPDATE: Guess I was wrong about the handle lasting, it didn't. I still use it for now but plan on replacing it with a similar cooler called Igloo Quantum. This may be an updated version of the ice cube model who knows. The handle feels better but attaches the same so i expect it to fail as well. It has a few additional features like 2 places to put a lock or locks on it, useless because it can be easily cut. 2 cup holders that I find too shallow to be useful and the top compartment is half the size. The cover is thicker and opens easier from the center as opposed to the corners like the ice cube model. Lastly; it's 3 tone. Had I know the Quantum was available I would have purchased it over the ice cube model. In my opinion, they should lose the cup holders and increase the top compartment size, ensure the handle wont come off and you would have a great cooler.
text_fidelity_b: Igloo Ice Cube, Ocean Blue, 14-can Capacity, 32607

Disappointed that the other review steered me wrong, hopefully my honest review will set things right.  Felt so strongly about this review that I uploaded a video of this clamp "sticking" and the rust stain on the clamping surface.  Footnote: I did pick up the Rising Ultralight and it does operate much more smoothly, as well as appearing to be made of a higher quality metal.

text_fidelity_a:
Noggn Bike, Skateboard, Scooter Helmet for Adult, Youth, Teens | Medium-Large for Men, Women, Boys and Girls 14+ | 5 Designs: Rainbow Unicorn, US Star, Tropical, Beach, Mountains | The first thing you will immediately notice about this helmet is the brightness of the color scheme. The pink is very vibrant and the rainbow colors pop. It is also very shiny. Having the bright colors and the glossy shine definitely adds to the safety because it should make you stand out more while you are participating in an activities that require a helmet. Also, good for parents because the kids will enjoy the look and can easily spot you while you ride ahead.

The fit is nice, it is comfortable to wear, has good ventilation and it is lightweight. You can adjust the circumference size (turning a nob inside the helmet) and the straps that buckle to secure the helmet on your head. Even though this helmet looks like it would be nice for a child, it is definitely an adult (or older kid/ teenager) sized helmet. It easily fit two average adult heads. One nice feature is that it comes with a detachable cushion that helps pad the strap pressed against the underside of the neck/throat area. Very nice touch on the extra cushion. A bonus is that you can remove and easily wash it.

Please note that this helmet is not intended to provide protection while participating in motorized sports such as a moped. There are no details on a maximum speed that you should avoid. To be safe I would only use this helmet for bike riding, skating, ect.

It comes with a one month warranty, but you can email the company to extend the warranty to one year.

Great colorful and fun helmet!

This helmet is Made in China and being sold by a Canadian company on Amazon. At the current price it's a bit expensive for what it is. . . but. . . I like it.
text_fidelity_b: Noggn Bike, Skateboard, Scooter Helmet for Adult, Youth, Teens | Medium-Large for Men, Women, Boys and Girls 14+ | 5 Designs: Rainbow Unicorn, US Star, Tropical, Beach, Mountains |

It pretty much works as advertised, but-battery life and magnet strength in Xmitter is questionable. The sender has to be about 1-2 mm from the battery. That's a pretty tight fit, esp with carbon front forks. As the battery on the sender weakens, there's no real communication from it to tell what the problem is (I got a "Too Many Signals" error). On the computer unit, Temperature gauge isn't accurate, reads way too high, and there doesn't seem to be any way to calibrate it. The manual is thorough and detailed, but somehow confusing (What can I say? It's written by English speakers, not English thinkers)
On the positive side, The readout is very clear; you can do individual parameter resets, the rubber bands (o-rings really) are pretty tough, I haven't broken one yet, and it has a dual mount, stem or handlebar, which was very important for me, as I put safety brakes on my handle bar, which ate up real estate. At 120 bucks, it's pricey, but at 83? IMO that's getting into bargain territory for the feature set.

text_fidelity_a:
Firmstrong Bruiser Man Single Speed Beach Cruiser Bicycle This bike has turned out to be a very good purchase for me.

I live on my boat in Los Angles and am able to attend to 90% of my brick and mortar shopping without using my car since this bike is beefy and has no problem handling a couple of saddle bag type baskets as well as a basket on the handlebars. A 36 pack of canned beer rides securely on the rear rack held in place with bungee cords

I bought the three speed model and am glad I did. Even though the area around us is pretty flat there are a few sloped ramps, on our great local bike paths, that make me appreciate the ability to shift down. Down wind on a level surface, or down hill, the high gear is useful. Some days the breeze off the ocean is strong enough to cause me to shift down when headed up wind. The three speed has no derailleur so the bike has a chain guard.

This bike is very easy to ride and takes a lot of the back and hand stress out of riding my bike. Im 72 and outgrew dropped handlebars about half a century ago.

It took me a few days to get used to coaster brakes again, after decades of cool bikes with hand brakes. But now Im cool with the coaster brake and really like the lack of clutter on the handle bars.

I added a bell, lights and a holder for my smart phone. I also added a really nice rear view mirror which is a great safety feature. I got a nice beefy lock on Amazon and really like the fact that I can drop it in my basket instead of going to the trouble of installing it on the mount on the bike every time I take off.

Since I live in southern California fenders seemed pointless so I skipped that accessory.

The bike is easy to ride with its big tires but is not fast. If you want a fast bike a beach cruiser is probably not what you should buy.

Unless I have some compelling reason to get in my car I do all my local travel on my bike. Its easier, faster many times, and there are no parking hassles or cost. I rode it 25 miles round trip to a doctor appointment a week ago. It was along the beach where there is a nice bike path and lots of scenery. It was not an exhausting experience but then I was not in a big hurry.

As I ride to the gym every morning Im passed by cyclists on high tech bikes who are bent into incredibly uncomfortable looking positions over their dropped handle bars. As they zoom past I reflect on the fact that I definitely bought the right bike for me and also that some people should not be wearing lycra cycling outfits.

The only negative about this purchase was that the packaging on the bike was not adequate to protect it in shipment. The three speed shifter on the rear axel had broken through the cardboard box and got scratched up in shipment. The damage did not look like it was more than cosmetic and I did not want o hassle with repacking the bike to return it so I went ahead and accepted as it was.
text_fidelity_b: Firmstrong Bruiser Man Single Speed Beach Cruiser Bicycle

I've not used the additional logs for food, heart rate, blood glucose, and blood pressure.  No huge surprise that I'm too sedentary.  The surprise was with my sleep.  I would have sworn I was getting more sleep and sleeping like a log.  Flex tells me the brutal truth that I am way below the amount of sleep I need and am way more restless during the little sleep I do get.  I am trying slowly, but surely, to increase the amount of sleep I get.  I have a bit of frustration while gardening because some of my activities create enough vibration to cause the device to think I'm going to sleep.  I've worn it in the shower from the beginning and everything still works well.  In fact, the only time I've removed it except for recharging was for a formal event (and only because I could not find a bracelet that would camouflage it well enough!!).  I would recommend this device.  It gives you a reality check and could motivate you to make some adjustments for a healthier lifestyle.  It gets 4 stars instead of 5 simply because it can't tell when I'm gardening.  :-)
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Flex Wireless Activity + Sleep Wristband, Black, Pedometer, Small/Large

text_fidelity_a:
Optimus - Hiker Plus Single Unit The only reason this stove did not get a five star rating is because it arrived in a sealed box almost fully disassembled. None of the screws or twist on fittings were still attached. The tank pivot screws were both loose inside as were the tank and heat shield floating around in the box. The tank cap was also loose as was the pump collar. In addition a lot of these have faulty NRVs (None Reverse Valves) whihc keep pressure from the tank backing into the pump and either leaking fuel or pushing the pump plunger back out after you have pumped it up. I would have thought a conscientious seller would hear all the little parts rattling around inside and done something.

This is both an engineering flaw and assembly failure to not have these things tight enough to make it to the customer. It took some time to assemble it properly as the parts diagram doesn't have enough detail to tell what order things went under the tank pivots. You have to search the internet and find what was next to the tank, bracket and shield arms. Then you MUST USE THREAD LOCK to keep this from happening again as the screws are too short and don't bottom out before being tight. When the tank is slid in and out of the stove it turns the screws and eventually they will come loose again. They should have used shoulder screws or longer screws like on previous models, then they could be fully tightened and left that way. Once it was properly assembled and the threads on the tank pivots locked and the NRV removed, repaired and replaced and properly tightened, all was good with the world.

Now to the stove. This is NOT a backpacking stove. It is a brick! You would think with the name "Hiker" it would be pretty light like the Svea 123 which is a little miracle, but not. However it is indestructible when properly assembled. The burner is very hot and also pretty noisy. The pot supports are widely spaced but most pots will fit without a problem. The stove has no feet, just the flat bottom of the case. You may need to use little rocks/sticks to keep it from wobbling.

Now to it's use. First it can use several fuels but not with equal ease. Choices are Naphtha (Coleman White Gas Fuel), Kerosene 1K, Diesel or if you have some laying around Jet Fuel, which is somewhat like Kerosene.

There is a bit more of a trick to lighting it without losing your eyebrows or hair for that matter. Until you get blue flame you have to meter the throttle often. First pump it up until you start to feel increased resistance, about 20 - 50 strokes. The plunger does not stay in after the last stroke like Coleman appliances. It works it's way back out about half way. That is normal. Now hold a flame to the bottom of the burner FIRST if you can and open the throttle until it lights then turn it back down and wait. Either the flame will start to die after a bit or you will start hearing the hissing of the stove starting to generate. Either way start opening the valve slowly again and let it create a flame about 6 inches high but not higher or the fuel can start running all over the bottom of the case and you will have a bonfire. As the flame starts hissing and turning blue you can start opening the valve more and more until you have a constant blue roaring flame. You are good to go now. You will need to add a few pumps as the flame goes down now and then.

When you are done close the valve and let the whole thing cool a few minutes, them push the pump in and slide the tank in. Drop the valve knob inside and snap the lid closed. If is going to sit more than a few months drain it.

Fuels: Although it will burn all listed, some work better than others. Also outside temperature has an effect on each fuel's performance. White gas is fastest to light and Diesel for fastest boil. Kerosene is a good middle point. Diesel.takes a LOOOOOOONG time to light. I didn't have any Jet A. Remember when changing fuels to drain the old fuel well and give it a quick rinse and drain with a couple ounces of the new fuel before filling.

Here are some fuel comparisons I made on a 90 degree day:

Fuel - Light time to max - Boil time for 2C tap water from tap temp
White Gas - 1 1/2 minutes - 3:15 minutes/seconds
Kerosene/Klean Heat* - 3 minutes and can bee sooty - 2:30 minutes/seconds
Diesel - 5 minutes ** - 2 minutes

* Klean Heat is a "Klean Strip" brand odorless Kerosene substitute. I like it for indoor wick lanterns as it gives off much less odor and is very clean burning. However in pressure stoves I don't see a difference in either odor or performance.

** I could not get the Diesel to burn a full blue flame. There were always yellow tips and it was not fully efficient as evidenced by the soot on the bottom of the pot. This is the only fuel which did this. I checked with the manufacturer and they said this is normal as Diesel is the dirtiest fuel. They recommended white gas as having the least problems and maintenance in the long run.

Enjoy your rugged little gas stove. It should last you a lifetime and still have life in it with proper maintenance.
text_fidelity_b: Optimus - Hiker Plus Single Unit

I wasted my $6 to get her spooled up with line but the worst part I didn't get to try out my new reel on father's day - I was really excited to use it! I'm glad I didn't get the other spool loaded up with braided line like I was thinking - I'd have been out another $30...
If the Kastking people make good on the replacement I'll test it out and will consider changing my rating. Right now I'm disappointed and wanted to gripe. Anticlimactic!
Is this rare or typical? We'll find out! Looking at other ratings seems like it might be rare (I hope). I'll update as things progress. - Wayne

text_fidelity_a:
POLAR FT60 Heart Rate Monitor Round TWO! I'd bought this identical HRM kit back in February 2014. From day one, I'd get WILDLY erratic readings on the heart rate - but that's ok, cuz I am actually from Planet Mars. No machine in any gym, nor any kind of heart rate monitor on Planet Earth works consistently on me. I either get zero reading (when my Martian paws are on the piece of exercise equipment) or I get rates that jump from 189 to 60 to 132, and so on. Don't tell the NSA, because I'm here on a secret mission: to see if my second purchase of this Polar FT60 HRM works. I should've registered my initial purchase back in Feb, but being a foolish optimist, I used the HRM daily - till it plain died on me long about August. I stopped getting any kind of reading between the transmitter and the device - even after new batteries were inserted. So I assumed it was a goner.

What I LOVE about this HRM:
- It gives me the data I need to stick with my fitness program: how many minutes spent in zone 1, 2, & 3 (based on initial VO2 reading and the 6-min fitness test I took first time I took it to the gym); my total calories burned and what percentage of them were fat; my average and max heart rate (which, on the first device I purchased gave the "accurately" bizarre ranges of 189 to 62, but I know why that is). That is ALL I need to know. I'm not a marathon runner or even daily runner. My goal is to burn 400+ calories in a variety of ways at the gym (or outdoors) on most days of the week. I don't need to know my footfall, cadence, how much foot is on the ground every nano-second, my GPS coordinate, or about 100 other functions that other HRMs provide (and which are no doubt of interest to the athlete wearing them).
- It's easy to find your VO2 (well, maybe it's based on a lame algorithm, but I have SOME number to work with)
- It's compatible with ALL the machines in my gym, so I don't have to keep looking down at my wrist every few seconds (like I did with the Garmin) to see what my heart rate is - a BIG plus!
- It's pretty intuitive to operate, once you spend 5 min learning the main buttons.
- It's a good-looking watch
- It doesn't drain the battery like some of the Garmin devices (unless you shut off GPS and turn the device off)

What I HATE about the device (Product Development: READ ME FIRST)
- the buttons are CRIPPLINGLY PAINFUL to press. It's ridiculous, but no kidding, I had to press the dang buttons against a flat, hard piece of granite counter to actually get them to depress.
- OUCH! OUCH! OUCH! OUCH! OUCH! I have short nails, but they'd just slip off the button if I used them, so I use the fleshy tip of my now CRIPPLED, broken finger to press the idiotically STIFF buttons on this watch. I mean come ON: spend a nickel more and get some decent springs under these buttons, so I don't get arthritis from pressing them every day.
- These painful buttons drove me to THROW the whole kit away when it stopped working (my duh) and go buy a Garmin HRM right here at Amazon.com. Unfortunately, that device seems to require a PhD in Rocket Science to call up the right screens to find the few bits of data I was interested in. PLUS that device also gave very erratic readings, given that it was not made for a Martian, but rather an Earthling.
- I think that for the money paid, the Polar FT60 should *in theory* last longer than a scant 6 mos? The warranty is for 2 years, but I've read elsewhere (mostly from a few years back) that other folks complained about their device conking out.

I'm going to register this HRM and take good care of it, cuz despite the NUMBINGLY PAINFUL buttons, it is the only device that gives me the exact data I want to see after each workout.

Please Polar: Make these buttons easier to press, huh?
text_fidelity_b: POLAR FT60 Heart Rate Monitor

Fitness Reality Squat Rack Power Cage with | Optional LAT Pulldown & Leg Holdown Attachment | Squat and Bench Rack Combos| Super Max 810 XLT | I'm extremely pleased with the product. Assembly was straightforward and all the holes lined up! Very sturdy construction.

The attached pictures show an addition I made to turn give the rack a cable-crossover functionality. These pictures represent my Version 1.0.

All the parts can be purchased at Lowes. The rack has two perfect attachment points for the pulleys. See picture 1. This shows a threaded eye bolt and 1 1/2" fixed pulley. Two lock nuts hold it in place but it is purposely NOT tight so it has the ability to rotate. Picture 2 shows a length of zinc coated square steel tubing from Lowes. Three threaded eye bolts connect the additional cables to the center cable on the rack. Picture 3 shows me pulling on the two handles.

I think this works really well. Keep in mind, this is Version 1. One could probably cut the steel tubing length down. With the full length, it doesn't seem to hit the cage but it potentially could. NOTE: I did try this without the steel tubing and I didn't like the feel. As one completes the motion, the angle change in the cables was significant enough to notice. Your mileage may vary and you may prefer that characteristic. That tubing was the most expensive piece at about $20. Everything else is dirt cheap.

If you decide to try something like this, please be EXTREMELY careful. I am a Mechanical Engineer by education so this was something I was comfortable doing. Review the load limits of ALL the components you intend to use. For instance, the two fixed pulleys from Lowes have a safe working load of 420 pounds. I used 1/8" vinyl coated braided wire rope. Blue Hawk brand with a safe working load of 340 pounds.

Make sure ANY carabiners you use to make connections are rated for HIGH LOAD and NOT for hanging keys on your belt loop. I can't stress this enough. You do NOT want something breaking on you during full extension.

IMPORTANT: Make sure you terminate the ends of the cables correctly. Properly swaged deformable collars are likely the best approach but I used a threaded clamp for this setup. I will likely change to a swaged connection because the clamping hardware can rub against your arm during use. Also, use thimbles on the ends of both cables to protect the cable attachment points.
text_fidelity_b: Fitness Reality Squat Rack Power Cage with | Optional LAT Pulldown & Leg Holdown Attachment | Squat and Bench Rack Combos| Super Max 810 XLT |

text_fidelity_a:
KEEPTO Exercise Resistance Band Set with Handles,5 Fitness Workout Bands for Women at Home Gym We have a large array of options for working out - to loose/keep off weight and build and maintain muscle. But among the options we wanted something that we could travel with as well as give us a variety of options at home. Boredom can kill a workout routine.

I specifically chose this set for 1. the variety and choices of weights, 2. The options for use with/without a door, 3. The look of the hand and ankle straps and handles, 4. The look of the ends of the bands - their connector including the carabiner connectors.

1. The variety of weights/resistance allows one to go up to 120 lbs. We are not there, but we have the option. Changing the bands out can give a range of weight options and this was a good one compared to others. It also lets one adjust what they are doing - legs, arms.

2. The options for use with or without a door means one can anchor the bands under one’s foot or in a door. We have a TRX set we use with a door, but this gives us another option - we would be more likely to travel with this set now so if unable to use in a door on a trip we would still have the ability to use our feet. That said, there is something “better” to a TRX version. It feels stronger - but it is slightly heavier, while this set is more complicated with all the items included.

3. The hand and ankle straps appeared average overall, but better than some other sets we were looking at. The handles are a bit “rough,” but not uncomfortable. I have worked them with and without gloves and both are fine. The ankle straps are average in feel, but better than some I’ve experienced. Overall both are just fine.

4. I was mostly concerned that they would have longevity. I looked at how the bands connected to the handles, how they were topped off to keep their own ends secure. Compared to others - via pictures - these appeared to have good, solid endings, and that the make up of how they connect to the handles was a good method. I know the carabiners are the weakest link and I took that into consideration. I think they are pretty solid - based on pictures and how they feel - but I am prepared should they fail - we would be able to change them out for others if needed.

Overall we are happy with this choice. The set is what it appears to be, but compared to many others - and I looked at more than 20 sets - this one had everything we wanted, feels as though it has the longevity and strength we wanted and expect, and will give us another successful workout option.

Happy to recommend.
text_fidelity_b: KEEPTO Exercise Resistance Band Set with Handles,5 Fitness Workout Bands for Women at Home Gym

text_fidelity_a:
The Skill Board Mini Beginner to Pro - Wooden Balance Board for Adults Bundle - Incl. Balance Trainer for All Sports, Gym, Standing Desk, or Yard Games, 2x Fitness Balls, Ball Pump and more First, I have to admit, we only used this The Skill Board Mini Beginner to Pro - Wooden Balance Board for Adults Bundle once since arriving. It arrived at the same point my wife and I got sick (we’ve been down for a few weeks), so it’s been in the corner since unpacking and had only one test run. My pics would normally be of the product fully unwrapped and ready for use and/or in use.

But in these pictures you see the size of the bundle included. Pictures of the set show the number of pieces including the two balls, the cushion, and the board (dark brown flat item), and thickness of the board. “Out of the box,” if you will, this The Skill Board Mini Beginner to Pro - Wooden Balance Board for Adults Bundle is a great deal with multiple pieces offering an athlete or anyone working out several options - the cushion is about our speed for beginning, but I know with the balls you can make it harder or easier based on how big the ball is you choose to use, or how much you fill it. The number of items included in the bundle alone makes it a great deal in our book. We have had a previous, similar workout board that only included the board and cushion (to be fair, it was half the price), but while we truly enjoyed that set, we were unable to move up if we wanted without buying more. So that you get as much here as you do is a plus.

We only unwrapped the cushion and platform for our initial test run, and found them both to be excellent for our needs. The thickness of the board made us both comfortable and with a listed weight up to 300 lbs., even with the extra weight I’m working off I am safe and comfortable on the board. We found the cushion to be easy to get inflated and hold the air. Having had one before we knew how to use it and were quickly getting on and off and balancing. We always use ours for both standing on and as a platform for planking and like the challenge. We have not (as of yet) put the non-skid surface on (again, we’ve been down), but have not decided either way if we’ll use it, but we have it for when we are ready.

We are also looking forward to trying the two balls. At this point neither of us is comfortable yet to try, so we’re unable to speak to it, but we love that this is an option to move into once we are ready. In the end we are very pleased with the bundle and feel this The Skill Board Mini Beginner to Pro - Wooden Balance Board will help us get back up and going once we are recovered. Just that test run reminded us how much we love this kind of core workout and how well it worked for us in the past. We’re happy to be able to do this again and believe the The Skill Board Mini Beginner to Pro - Wooden Balance Board for Adults Bundle will be great moving forward.
text_fidelity_b: The Skill Board Mini Beginner to Pro - Wooden Balance Board for Adults Bundle - Incl. Balance Trainer for All Sports, Gym, Standing Desk, or Yard Games, 2x Fitness Balls, Ball Pump and more

text_fidelity_a: ENGERWALL Fitness Tracker with Step Counter/Calories/Stopwatch, Activity Tracker with Heart Rate Monitor, IP68, Health Tracker with Sleep Tracker, Smartwatch, Pedometer Watch for Women Men Kids When I got this, I was so excited. It was easy to use, and really encouraged me. I have high blood pressure, so I thought that the 10 thousand steps I was doing every day somehow lowered it. Then I went to my doctor, and found that my blood pressure was higher than ever, despite the fact that the watch said it was below normal. So I took my blood pressure at the doctors office at the same time I took it with the watch. Three times the numbers were drastically different. Then, just out of curiosity, I carefully counted my steps to see if the watch came up with the same number. Not even close.  This is a great tool if you are looking for a way to boost your confidence and self esteem without having to actually improve anything--you know, kind of like the filters in photoshop that make you look thinner and younger. However, if you are wanting accurate information, skip this watch and find one that tells you the truth about your health and fitness.

My wife has been using such tiny charing ports for years (like us all) and she’s very careful. This thing easily popped off and in spite of her dainty skills at repairing such tiny things, cannot get it back on. That’s a minus for us.

But as a tool, it’s great. So if they can fix that flaw in how the port cover is attached, we’d be happy to give it a 5.

It arrived in a nice box (for yourself or a gift) in 3 parts: light, clamp, and charger. She charged right away - after as she pushed the piece in it popped off - and we put it on. She severely broke her foot a couple weeks ago and gets around for the next 3 months on a scooter. But she wants to be able to see at night if she’s moving through the house, or if we are outside, so we thought a bike light might work. It’s perfect for that. It fits on the handles of her scooter as easily as a bike - and we plan on switching it to a bike when she’s recovered. In the mean time, the 3 levels of light mean she can see safely in the house without being disruptive, and she can see safely outside moving to the car or around our home. It’s really easy to clamp and remove - she takes it off when we are in the car so it won’t get broken off. And she can easily pop it back on.

Overall this is a great light and minus the flaw with the port cover, we are really happy with it. That we cannot overlook, however, because there is little doubt that in 12+ weeks on the scooter and future use on the bike, covering the port hole would be a safety issue (rain). So the 4 star has to stay. Happy to have it though.

text_fidelity_a:
Ultimate Survival Technologies BlastMatch Fire Starter Obviously, judging by my profile name, I'm a girl. When it is time for me to start a fire, I need something that works right the first time with my smaller hands and does not break all my short but feminine nails. I have used a number of strikers and fire starters with hilariously varying results. Most are okay-ish. I don't like skinny little strikers that you have to rub with a piece of hacksaw blade which often has a back side that is almost as sharp and jagged as the business end of the blade. I don't like short micro strikers where you end up lighting your hangnails on fire along with the tinder because your hand was so close. (This doesn't actually happen but you get the picture.)

When I first bought this BlastMatch my husband immediately claimed it as his and it disappeared from the face of the earth for over two years. That should have been my first clue that it was the best striker out there. Every once in awhile it would resurface to light the fire pit in the back yard but it would quickly be whisked away to a back pocket and once again vanish from existence as rapidly as it had reappeared. I had no idea where he was hiding it so I simply had to resort to using other strikers I had purchased that worked well enough. They just were not as quick and easy as this one.

Let's talk about what I love. First of all, it has a big, thick firesteel rod that is the thickest I own. (See the picture I uploaded.) This means it will most likely last for the advertised number of strikes. Second, my son has been able to use this to start a fire on our camp outs since he was 7. It's really, really easy. to use. Not really that easy to open but you quickly get the hang of it. Basically you open it, use your thumb to depress the metal scraper on one side and then push down. A bright yellow, orange and white colored shower of sparks will greet you like an angry sparkler gone awry and set alight anything remotely resembling tinder. (A friend who first demonstrated his to us set the fine fibers of our living room rug on fire. After tamping out the little glowing embers, we were sold.)

My husband confiscated the first one I bought and would not so much as let me lay eyes on it so I decided to buy myself a second one. I had given the other crappy fire rods we had somehow picked up along the way to my boy scout son, which was surprisingly safe since they don't hardly light a thing, and proceeded to replace them all with a tool that worked. Since we have one BlastMatch from 2014 and one from 2016, I decided I would compare them side-by-side to see if the product has had any visible changes or become more flimsy as reviewers have insisted. I couldn't find a single difference. The plastic on each was the same thickness, the rod was the same diameter and they both opened with the same springy force.

They give a generous shower of sparks and if you get it anywhere close to a tinder ball, you are going to start a fire with one push. It catches that easily. I am very pleased with BOTH purchases and will continue to use these until they break. (If they do, I'll be right back here to complain.) While we don't use our BlastMatch every single day, we have used the original one somewhere around 50 or more times since my husband is a scout leader and it is still going strong with no cracks in the plastic and no damage visible anywhere to the striker. If you want to be on the safe side, wait until the price drops to twelve or less and then make your purchase. I have seen them as low as ten at various times of the year so your patience can pay off. And do not use your BlastMatch while drunk or trying to impress women. Not that the reviewers who broke theirs were either drunk or able at all to impress women - I'm just giving you some general good advice.

I bought both of my strikers at full price. I do not work for BlastMatch. I don't even particularly like catching things on fire. I just like roasting marshmallows. And Starburst. Happy camping everyone!
text_fidelity_b: Ultimate Survival Technologies BlastMatch Fire Starter

text_fidelity_a:
SABRE Stun Gun 3-In-1 Safety Tool, 1.154 Microcoulombs (µC) Charge, 115 dB Personal Alarm, Audible Up To 1,000-Feet (305-Meters), 70 Lumen Flashlight, Includes Wrist Strap The LED light is bright enough to help you get your key into a lock, but it'll only dimly light your path. The alarm sound is not very loud--not as loud as a car alarm or a whistle or a smoke alarm. It doesn't help that the speaker is on the back, where your hand naturally covers it to some degree. It makes a weird noise that didn't even grab the attention of a man sitting 70 feet away because it sounded like just another mechanical noise rather than an alarm. The stun gun made more noise! Personally, I'd hoped the light and the alarm noise would warn most potential attackers away, but I doubt they'll be much help. Since the light and the sound aren't as impressive as they advertised, I do wonder if the stun gun will be very effective, but I'm not going to test it out on anyone! They say it's most effective on certain parts of the body, so you have to be close and even aim somewhat, not just touch the current to some body part.

Anyway, you get a USB charging cord and have to charge the stun gun 12 hours before the first use and 4-5 hours each week. Though the green (full charge indicator) light turns on after only a couple hours, they stress the length of time spent on charging more than the indicator light. There is an on/off switch than must be turned on before the alarm sound or the stun gun button will work. The light button will work at all times. The buttons are easy to use, though the labeling on them is not easy to read (especially at night). The light stays on until pressed off, which means it can be turned on if something presses the button when in your purse. This could run the battery down so it's not effective when needed. Some way to check how much charge is left would have been useful. I've never seen or used a stun gun before, but this seemed more hype than useful.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Stun Gun 3-In-1 Safety Tool, 1.154 Microcoulombs (µC) Charge, 115 dB Personal Alarm, Audible Up To 1,000-Feet (305-Meters), 70 Lumen Flashlight, Includes Wrist Strap
